claims.claim: 2026 monthly income tax brackets: up to 7,010 at 10%; 7,011-10,060 at 14%; 10,061-19,000 at 20%; 19,001-25,100 at 31%; 25,101-46,690 at 35%; 46,691-60,130 at 47%; 60,131 and above at 50% (47% plus the 3% surtax). The surtax threshold is annual income above 721,560 NIS. The bracket widening was enacted in the 2026 budget and applies retroactively from January 2026.

2026 Bituach Leumi and health-tax EMPLOYEE rates. The standard row (able-bodied resident aged 18 to retirement, not drawing an old-age pension, not a controlling shareholder) is NI 1.04% / health 3.23% up to the reduced-collection threshold of 7,703 NIS/month, and NI 7.00% / health 5.17% above it, totalling 4.27% and 12.17%. Maximum insurable income is 51,910 NIS/month. The official table has other employee rows with different rates, including a controlling shareholder at 4.25% / 11.96%, an employee over 70 or drawing a disability pension at 3.23% / 5.17%, a 67-to-70-year-old not drawing an old-age pension at 3.93% / 10.03%, a new resident over 62 and under retirement age at 3.60% / 7.45%, and an employee under 18 or drawing an old-age pension who pays no employee contribution.

claims.claim: Section 45a gives salaried employees a 35% income-tax credit on their pension contribution, on a qualifying contribution capped at 8,148 NIS/year (~679 NIS/month, 7% of a ~9,700 NIS qualifying salary), for a maximum annual credit of ~2,851.8 NIS (~238 NIS/month off income tax).

Section 47 is not self-employed-only, but it is means-tested. For a salaried employee with unpensioned salary components (overtime, company-car imputed value, commissions), a deposit against that slice earns a Section 47 deduction plus a Section 45a credit only where insured salary is at or below 24,250 NIS/month in 2026. Above that, no Section 47 deduction is available and only a credit remains, at 5% of the unpensioned income and not above the 9,700 NIS qualifying ceiling. Worked example from the source: an employee on 30,000 NIS of which 25,000 is pensioned may deposit 5% of the 5,000 unpensioned slice, 250 NIS/month or 3,000 NIS/year, and receives a 35% credit of 1,050 NIS under Section 45a (סעיף 45א).

claims.claim: Section 102 capital-gains track: 25% capital-gains rate, 24-month trustee holding period measured from the GRANT date. The 102(b)(3) ordinary-income split applies ONLY to a company whose shares are already traded, or which lists within 90 days of the grant, and is measured as the average share price over the 30 trading days before the grant less what the employee paid. For a grant in a private company the whole benefit can be capital at 25%. A benefit on the capital-gains track is not employment income and so carries no Bituach Leumi and no health tax, but it does count toward the 3% surtax threshold.

claims.claim: Keren hishtalmut: employee 2.5% and employer 7.5% is the standard tech split, tax-exempt growth after six years, and the tax-qualifying ceiling for 2026 is 188,544 NIS/year, i.e. 15,712 NIS/month. The employer's exemption is additionally capped at three times the employee's own contribution, so a 7.5% / 2.5% split sits exactly at that limit and an employee-side reduction breaks it. At the 15,712 NIS ceiling the maximum tax-benefited employer deposit is 1,178 NIS/month (1,178.4 exactly) at 7.5%, the maximum employee deposit is 392.8 NIS/month at 2.5%, and the combined employer-plus-employee maximum at 10% is 1,571 NIS/month (1,571.2 exactly).
claims.raw_snippet: ולא יותר מפי 3 מחלקו של העובד בהפרשות

claims.claim: An employer keren hishtalmut deposit above the qualifying ceiling (15,712 NIS/month, 188,544/year in 2026) is treated as the employee's income at the moment of deposit and is taxed at the employee's marginal bracket. The employer's exemption is also capped at 3x the employee's own contribution. On a 40,000 NIS base with a 7.5% employer rate this imputes 1,822 NIS/month, costing roughly 638 NIS/month in tax at a 35% marginal rate and reducing real net-to-bank from about 23,100 to about 22,450 NIS.

claims.claim: Mandatory pension from January 2017 totals 18.50% of salary, split 6.00% employee, 6.50% employer tagmulim and 6% employer severance. The employer tagmulim rate includes work-disability cover. The 8.33% severance rate used across Israeli tech is a Section 14 (סעיף 14) arrangement pre-funding one month per year, above the 6% statutory severance, which is what makes the tech employer stack 14.83% rather than the statutory 12.5%. The salary on which mandatory pension is due is the average wage, 13,769 NIS in 2026.

claims.claim: The statutory employer pension and severance floor is 6.5% pension plus 6% severance, i.e. 12.5% of gross, within a total mandatory 18.50% split 6.00% employee / 6.50% employer / 6% severance. The 14.83% figure used in tech reflects a full Section 14 arrangement with severance at 8.33% (one month per year) rather than the statutory 6%.

Private-sector recuperation pay (dmey havra'a) for havra'a year 2026 is 451.5 NIS per day, updated on 18.08.2026 from the previous 418 NIS, with employers who already paid at 418 owing the difference. Public sector is 511.6 NIS per day.
